judged_text: The same sync Response is handed to consumers with incompatible expectations — Google reads .data, Hubspot reads flat token fields, Zoho reads axios-style .data, Lark's handleLarkError validates Lark's {code,msg,data} envelope, Webex/Zoom/O365 parse provider-specific token schemas — while the comment promises 'the response should only contain the access token and expiry date'. No single sync-endpoint response shape can satisfy all callers, so self-hosters enabling sharing get apps that crash or silently store incomplete credentials depending on which provider they use, and a contract-compliant parent (access token + expiry only) guarantees breakage for the fetch-native apps whose parsers expect provider-specific fields.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens()` which, when sharing is enabled, returns a *fetch `Response` from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`* regardless of what the caller normally expects (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Multiple call sites then treat that return value as incompatible shapes: Google expects `.data` from the returned object (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: `const token = res?.data`), Zoho Bigin expects an axios response with `.data` (`zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`: `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)`), Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object (not a `Response`) (`hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`), etc. In sharing mode these will yield `undefined`/runtime errors (e.g., `tokenInfo.data` access on a fetch Response) or cause token parsing to fail (Google sets `access_token` from `token.access_token` where `token` is undefined, then `parseRefreshTokenResponse` will throw). This is a concrete, diff-verifiable behavioral break when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + sync endpoint are set.
